questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates proficiency in partition DP with non-additive segment scores (bitwise AND). It assesses understanding of precomputation strategies and solution reconstruction.

## Key Concepts
- DP for partitioning an array into k contiguous blocks
- Precomputing subarray AND values in O(n²) time
- Backtracking to reconstruct segment endpoints
- Time/space trade-offs

## Code Example
```python
def max_and_partition(A, k):
    n = len(A)
    andv = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        andv[i][i] = A[i]
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            andv[i][j] = andv[i][j-1] & A[j]
    
    dp = [[-float('inf')] * (k + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        dp[i][1] = andv[0][i-1]
    
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for t in range(2, min(k, i) + 1):
            for p in range(t - 1, i):
                dp[i][t] = max(dp[i][t], dp[p][t-1] + andv[p][i-1])
    
    return dp[n][k]
```

## Why This Is Asked
Explores a fresh DP angle: exact partition into k segments with a segment cost defined by range, forcing precomputation and backtracking to recover segment boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Range-based segment cost (max-min)
- Exact partition DP: dp[i][t]
- Precomputation of cost[l][r]
- Backtracking reconstruction

## Code Example
```javascript
// pseudocode for core DP (not complete):
for i in 1..n:
  dp[i][1] = cost[1][i]
for t in 2..k:
  for i in t..n:
    dp[i][t] = min_{l=t-1..i-1} dp[l][t-1] + cost[l+1][i]
    par[i][t] = argmin
```

## Follow-up Questions
- Can you optimize to O(nk) with divide-and-conquer if cost satisfies quadrangle inequality?
- How would you adapt for 0/1-based indexing and streaming inputs?
